# The Urlcade

> A self-hosted game-authoring API, delivered as a URL-encoded virtual
> console: build a cart as a plain JS object, encode it to bytes, and
> the resulting URL fragment *is* the game — decoded and run by a
> static, modular JS runtime shared by every cart. No server, no build
> step, no install, no account. Copy a link, the recipient gets the
> exact game. Designed to be self-serve for an AI agent: read
> AUTHORING.md, write a cart object, compile it and see specific errors
> at https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/compile/ — all without a
> human in the loop.

## Build a cart

- [AUTHORING.md](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/AUTHORING.md): How to build a cart — the object shape, every field's meaning, the opcode table, the hook lifecycle, the map generators. Start here.
- [kernel.js](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/kernel.js): The actual `encodeCart`/`decodeCart`/opcode table/assembler/VM/compression/disassembler — one dependency-free file, the single source of truth for the cart format (loaded directly, not copied, by the runtime, the Inspector, and /compile). Runs standalone under Node or any JS host: no browser, no network, no build step (`const K = require('./kernel.js')`).
- [fixtures.md](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/fixtures.md): Known-good (cart description → exact bytes → exact fragment string) examples generated by kernel.js. Check your own implementation against these directly — nothing here requires running anything.

## Compile it

- [/compile](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/compile/): Self-serve compiler and decompiler. Paste a cart source object (the same shape AUTHORING.md describes) and it compiles automatically — specific, line-numbered errors if a hook's assembly is wrong, a specific decode error if a pasted fragment is malformed — with a live Play/Inspect link the moment it succeeds. Paste a fragment instead and it decompiles back to source, disassembly included, editable and re-compilable in place. This is the fastest loop for an agent iterating on a cart: no server round-trip, no separate toolchain, just this page.

## Play it / inspect it

- [Play](https://canyonturtle.github.io/games/): The live runtime — five playable cartridges (Flappy Bird, a racer, a roguelike, a platformer, and a physics-based castle-crusher), and an INSPECT button on each that decodes and visualizes any cart (palette, sprites, tiles, map, entities, disassembled hooks) including ones you paste in yourself. Any validly-encoded cart fragment is directly playable at `/#<fragment>`, not only the five shipped carts — a link from /compile works exactly the same way as one of the shelf's own.
